title: Discourse Analysis of Legislative Bill Discussions
abstract: arXiv:2611.05381v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Legislative hearings are distinct communication events with their own human recognizable structure and logic, yet they have been analyzed as distinct phenomena beyond their transcripts. Understanding legislative hearings at a deeper level is a major step in analyzing the work and power relationships within democratic bodies. In this work, we present a novel end-to-end pipeline for parsing rhetorical structures from legislative committee hearings with the goal of improving legislative discourse analysis and democratic accountability. We also propose a rhetorical structure grammar and find that 55.21% of California state bill discussions in our dataset can be parsed with this grammar. We evaluate our pipeline with two utterance section classifiers on a random subset of over 2,000 annotated utterances corresponding to 100 hearings. We find that a logistic regression-based classifier with grammar-based output masking and utterance tag smooth

translated_title: 立法法案讨论的话语分析
translated_abstract: 立法听证会是独特的交流事件，具有人类可识别的自身结构和逻辑，然而以往的研究仅将其视为超越文字记录的独特现象来分析。在更深层次上理解立法听证会是分析民主机构内部工作与权力关系的重要一步。在这项工作中，我们提出了一个新颖的端到端流水线，用于从立法委员会听证会中解析修辞结构，旨在改进立法话语分析和民主问责。我们还提出了一种修辞结构语法，并发现我们数据集中55.21%的加州州法案讨论可以用该语法进行解析。我们在超过2000个标注话语（对应100场听证会）的随机子集上，使用两个话语片段分类器评估了我们的流水线。我们发现，基于逻辑回归的分类器结合基于语法的输出掩码和话语标签平滑方法……（原文此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出了一种用于解析立法委员会听证会修辞结构的端到端流水线和修辞结构语法，其中55.21%的加州州法案讨论可被该语法解析，从而改进了立法话语分析与民主问责。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel end-to-end pipeline and a rhetorical structure grammar for parsing rhetorical structures from legislative committee hearings, with 55.21% of California state bill discussions parseable by the grammar, thereby improving legislative discourse analysis and democratic accountability.
